overview.summary: APPROVED (ADR-0001) and IMPLEMENTED through PLAN-2026-0001 P2 (2026-09-28): Rust/Capy runtime with described operations, declared outputs, policy.json-only authority (deny-by-default), one `rivet serve` for REST/SSE/polling/WebSocket/MCP, the generated I/O manifest and least-privilege policy drafts, file CRUD, HTTP/1.1-2-3, TCP/Unix/WebSocket, processes with OS sandbox backends, UDP, QUIC, gRPC (four modes), OAuth 2.0 (three flows), MCP client connectors and sessions. Contract reconciled with the implementation at P2 exit (PLAN-2026-0001 TASK-086): use cases, ports, domain types, adapters, surfaces and flows are the implemented ones; todo texts keep the reviewed wording. Design deltas: scope_supervisor folded into execution_driver (with-block cleanup), policy_authenticator folded into the serve.authenticate_principal use case over policy.json; adapters added: h3_client, net_tls, remote_client, request_control, sandbox_linux/macos/unsupported, source_loader, wire_codec, effect_args. Re-reconciled after the post-P3 fix batches (Fix-A…D, 2026-09-28): audit.build_graph (rivet graph), trace export, per-request restrict, W3C traceparent, structured cancellation, secret taint on every sink, if/else, scoped file handles (files.open_file_stream), rivet.capabilities (registry.describe_capabilities), library scope/stream/duplex and host ceiling. PLAN-2026-0002 (v0.2.0, PROP-2026-0002 / ADR-0004) contract delta applied at P1 (TASK-004): one ResponseEnvelope and one InputEnvelope on every surface (serve.parse_input, legacy id/params aliases with deprecation signals), opt-in pretty JSON, immutable `global` constants (language.compile_globals), syntax highlighting (language.highlight_source), the `ffi` surface (C ABI through orchestrator/setup_ffi.rs) and the capability report's build features and ABI version.
overview.status: Runtime and Perch developer commands implemented. Perch command set approved by the maintainer on 2026-09-28; installation changed to bman add at the maintainer's explicit request; verified with the installed CLI, real release build/install, Rust checks, documentation checks and VHCO gates.
overview.why: Provide a root commands.perch that wraps existing Cargo, Python and VHCO workflows. Each command runs from ${script_dir}, declares cargo/bman/python3/vhco as optional binaries and CARGO_TARGET_DIR/CARGO_HOME/RUSTUP_HOME as optional environment variables, propagates failures, and uses the checked-in Cargo.lock for Cargo build/check/test/clippy/install. build produces the release binary; build_debug produces the debug binary; install first builds with cargo build --locked --release --bin rivet --target-dir ${script_dir}/target, then runs bman add with the quoted absolute ${script_dir}/target/release/rivet path (rivet.exe on Windows). The explicit target directory prevents CARGO_TARGET_DIR from selecting a different artifact; installation stops if the build fails and propagates bman failures. bman manages the global command destination. The main command prints available tasks (perch main, or the script-file invocation perch commands.perch); perch --help lists descriptions. Bare perch displays the installed CLI usage. The test wrapper is named tests because test is a reserved Perch built-in. gates runs fmt_check, check, clippy, tests, docs_check and architecture sequentially and stops on the first failure. Architecture runs vhco validate, sync and check; model/explorer generation remains explicit. clean removes Cargo build artifacts only when explicitly requested. No runtime feature, use case, port, surface, flow or domain delta is needed: these are developer wrappers outside the runtime model. Verification covers perch --check and --help, command dispatch from paths with spaces, Cargo environment forwarding, fail-fast gate behavior, release build/install, Rust formatting/type/lint/tests, documentation links and VHCO architecture/sync/guarantees. README.md and installation/contributor documentation describe the implemented tasks.
quickstart: # Perch interface approved by the maintainer on 2026-09-28.
perch main                         # print the command list
perch install                      # build release into ./target, then bman add the absolute binary path
perch architecture                 # vhco validate . -> vhco sync . -> vhco check .
perch gates                        # fmt_check -> check -> clippy -> tests -> docs_check -> architecture
perch docs                         # vhco doc . --format html (generated vhco.html)

use_cases.name: build_graph
use_cases.label: Show the static call graph
use_cases.about: Builds the static call graph of one operation from the compiled program and its effect catalog — literal (request …) calls expanded into the callee, connector calls, effect sites, DAG nodes with their after edges, and both arms of every if marked conditional; nothing is executed or evaluated.

todos.todo: the ID must name an operation, public unless `all`; a private or absent one is not_found.operation without disclosing which

structure (if/else arms with their condition, dag with nodes and after lists) comes from the IR; each effect site, literal call and connector call of the operation hangs under the innermost structure whose line range contains it, in source order; a call node expands the callee's graph unless the callee is already on the chain (cycle node)

failures.when: absent, or private without --all

use_cases.name: inspect_effects
use_cases.label: Generate the I/O manifest (inspect effects)
use_cases.about: Lists every effect site of the selected operations from the immutable compiled catalog — kind, access verbs, capability, normalized target, knowledge class, origin, phase and whether a file must already exist — grouped by operation, target or capability, optionally checked against the effective policy, joined to a request trace, or pre-flight probed on disk; nothing is executed and no source expression is evaluated.

todos.todo: Resolve the entry set: explicit ids, else every public operation visible to the query principal (the default); `all` adds private helpers and operations unreachable from any public entry. An unknown or private id without `all` is not_found (exit 4) without disclosing existence. `transitive` defaults to true: follow literal (request "id" ...) edges (and connector imports) and record each site's call_chain from the entry (e.g. [data.snapshot, data.read]); each site appears once per entry that reaches it. Nothing is executed and no source expression is evaluated.

Ask Registry.effect_sites for the lowered effect sites of each selected operation from the immutable compiled catalog (never re-parse, never connect). One source line can yield several sites and each is kept: `file update` = stat + update, `with file open ... mode read` = read, an MCP stdio call = process exec + mcp call, an MCP/gRPC HTTP call = network connect + mcp/grpc call, an OAuth `auth` attachment = env read of the client secret + credential read/write + auth use + token-endpoint connect + resource connect. Retain branch conditions, source spans and secrets (with the origins they are bound to). Classify knowledge as exact | bounded | param_dependent | dynamic | opaque_remote | opaque_native; a connector's remote side effects are opaque_remote, a native host callback is opaque_native. With include_bootstrap, list the fixed runtime-internal sites separately under `bootstrap` (bundle + imports, policy.json, CA bundle, resolv.conf/system resolver, tzdata, descriptor/schema files, stdin/stdout/stderr) which are never granted to scripts. Every file-valued option line is its own site (kind file, access [read], capability allow_read): `tls ca_file`, `tls cert_file`, `tls key_file` in http/with http/with websocket/with quic/with tcp blocks and in grpc/mcp(http transport) connectors (a connector's option sites appear under every operation that calls it), `body file PATH` and `body multipart` `file NAME PATH` upload sources and an operation-level `descriptor PATH`. Connector-level `descriptor`/`schema` files stay bootstrap reads (never granted to scripts) but carry the same fields.

Map every site to its access verbs and capability with the fixed table: file read|list|stat|watch -> allow_read; file create|update|append -> allow_write; file delete -> allow_delete; network connect -> allow_network (plus `protocol` http1|http2|http3|ws|sse|grpc|quic|udp|tcp and, for HTTP, `method` GET/POST/...; a WebSocket upgrade is connect with protocol ws); network bind|listen|multicast_join -> allow_listen; process exec -> allow_exec; env read -> allow_env; pipe read|write -> allow_pipe; unix connect|listen -> allow_unix; mcp call (tool|resource|prompt) -> allow_mcp; grpc call (unary|server_stream|client_stream|bidi) -> allow_grpc; auth use|manage|status -> allow_auth; credential read|write -> allow_credentials. Source verbs map one-to-one: `file create` -> create (exclusive), `file update` -> stat + update, `file delete` -> delete, `file list` -> list, `file read` -> read.

Give every site origin, phase, requires_existing and secret. origin = SiteOrigin{statement} for the statement that produced it (file read, file create, http get, with tcp, grpc, secret, command, ...) or SiteOrigin{option} for an option line (tls ca_file, tls cert_file, tls key_file, body file, descriptor, schema, endpoint, transport command). phase = load (bundle load/assembly: descriptor/schema, operation-level descriptor) | before_connect (read to build a connection: tls files) | connect (open a connection or spawn a process: network/unix connect, process exec) | body (statements and body options: file statements, body file, env read by secret, mcp/grpc calls, send/receive) | cleanup (finally blocks and scope disposal). requires_existing (file sites only; false otherwise) = true when the file must already exist when the operation starts (read, stat, list, update's stat and update, delete without `missing ok`, every option-derived read); false when the site creates it (create, write, append), when a missing file is tolerated (`missing ok`), or when the same operation creates the same normalized target earlier in source order (e.g. `file create ./out/report.json` then `body file ./out/report.json`). A missing requires_existing file fails at that site with not_found (exit 4); for load/before_connect files that happens before the block dials, so the block causes no effect. secret = true when the content read is secret material (tls key_file, env read by a `secret` statement); the path is always shown, the content is never read by inspection and is redacted in traces.

Normalize each target into SiteTarget{template, scheme, host, port, path, glob, params} and a normalized display string: URLs as scheme://host:port with the default port made explicit (https 443, wss 443) plus a path/query template where interpolations become {param} (e.g. https://api.example.com/users/{id}); file paths relative to the bundle root with {param} for interpolated segments and, for param_dependent paths, the derived glob (./out/notes/*.json); UDP/QUIC as udp://host:port or quic://host:port; env vars as `env NAME`; connector methods as connector/kind/name (crm/tools/search, users/example.Users/GetUser); auth as profile/account; processes as argv[0] plus argv template. `params` lists the caller parameters the target depends on; a target computed from a runtime value (e.g. a received datagram's peer) is dynamic and has no glob.

Only when check_policy is set: build an EffectIntent (capability, access, method, protocol, target) for each reachable site and ask PolicyEvaluator.evaluate against the effective policy (host ceiling ∩ loaded policy.json, or deny-by-default when absent) without performing I/O. decision = allowed when a grant covers target and every access verb and no deny matches; denied when no grant covers it, a deny matches, or a grant's `access` list omits a used verb; partial when a param_dependent target's derived glob is only partly covered by grants; unknown when the target itself cannot be matched (dynamic, opaque_native). An opaque_remote site whose endpoint or connector method is exact is evaluated normally; only its server-side effects stay outside the manifest (and make complete=false). Record the policy file's path and sha256 in the manifest.

Only when trace_request_id is given: read that request's trace from TraceStore (same live host or configured persistent store; otherwise not_found exit 4) and join TraceEvent.effect_id to EffectSite.effect_id, filling attempts {count, last_decision, last_phase} so planned and actual effects appear side by side; trace rows with no matching site are appended as unplanned.

Filter by kind and by access (a site matches when any of its verbs is in the requested list; an access verb that does not belong to the requested kind is validation, exit 2). Build TargetSummary rows by grouping sites on (normalized target origin/path-or-glob, capability) with the union of access verbs, HTTP methods and operation ids (a transitive user is listed as `X (via Y)`); a group's decision is the worst of its sites (denied > partial > unknown > allowed). `by` = operation (default; one row per site ordered by operation id then source line, a transitive call shown as its own `(calls X)` row), target (TargetSummary rows) or capability (TargetSummary rows under allow_read / allow_write / ... headings); any other value is validation (exit 2). TargetSummary also carries origins, phases and needs_file (yes | no | `yes: <verbs>` for a mixed row | null for non-file rows); the by=target table columns are TARGET ACCESS CAPABILITY ORIGIN PHASE NEEDS FILE USED BY.

Only when needs (or check_files) is set: build IoManifest.needs as one OperationNeeds per selected operation listing its file sites with requires_existing true as NeededFile{path, effect_id, origin, phase, secret, knowledge, via, source, status:null}; include callee needs reached through literal (request ...) calls with via = the callee id; drop files the same operation creates earlier; show param_dependent paths as their template with knowledge param_dependent. Static: no I/O. Bootstrap load files (descriptor/schema) are listed only with include_bootstrap, under a separate bundle-load group, because loading the bundle already proves they exist. The table form prints `<operation> needs, before it can run:` followed by `path (origin[, secret])` rows, or `<operation> needs no existing files.`; json returns the IoManifest with needs filled. rivet.io takes needs?: boolean and HTTP GET /v1/io?needs=true; check_files is CLI/library only and is never a network parameter.

Only when check_files is set (implies needs; CLI --check-files or IoQuery.check_files): for every exact NeededFile ask FileProbe.stat(FileProbeInput{path, effect_id, context}); the file_access adapter first authorizes the probe through PolicyEvaluator as allow_read with access stat (a grant with no access list covers stat) against the effective policy (host ceiling ∩ policy.json) and only then performs a metadata probe plus readability check, never opening or reading content (key files stay unread). Set status = present | missing | unreadable (exists but the OS denies this process read access) | not_permitted (policy does not grant stat; the path is not touched) | not_checkable (param_dependent or dynamic path; not probed). Print each status beside its row and a stderr summary. Exit code: 3 when any file is not_permitted or unreadable (permission, checked first); else 4 (not_found) when any required file is missing; else the normal io exit code.

Return IoReport{manifest, by, format, rendered, exit_code} whose manifest is IoManifest{bundle{file,sha256}, policy{file,sha256}|null, complete, sites, targets, bootstrap} with complete=false when any site is dynamic, opaque_remote or opaque_native. Render the requested format from the same data: table (fixed columns OPERATION KIND ACCESS TARGET KNOWLEDGE SOURCE [DECISION] [ATTEMPTS], TARGET ACCESS CAPABILITY ORIGIN PHASE NEEDS FILE USED BY for by=target, TARGET ACCESS USED BY under capability headings for by=capability, and the per-operation needs listing for needs/check_files), json (the IoManifest itself; HTTP GET /v1/io, MCP rivet.io and rt.io always return this form), markdown (the same tables as Markdown) or csv (one row per site). IoManifest also carries needs (empty unless needs/check_files). csv adds origin, phase, requires_existing and secret columns (origin as `statement:file read` / `option:tls key_file`). Exit code: 3 when check_policy found any reachable site denied or partial, or check_files found a file not_permitted or unreadable; else 4 when check_files found a required file missing; else 7 when strict and complete=false (inspection incomplete; never probe a remote endpoint to complete static analysis); else 0. Serve exposure: over the network rivet.io is callable only by a principal whose serve.principals.<name>.operations lists it explicitly; loopback principal local may call it.

use_cases.label: Read trace
use_cases.about: Returns one request's ordered broker decisions and attempts (each carrying its manifest effect_id) from the host's bounded trace store; reports eviction gaps instead of claiming complete, tamper-proof history.

todos.todo: Authorize trace access and validate cursor and byte limits before reading the selected request trace.
Read sanitized ordered events through TraceStore, preserving request, parent, node, attempt, policy and source IDs; report gaps and incomplete traces instead of claiming tamper proof history.

use_cases.name: acquire_credential
use_cases.label: Acquire credential
use_cases.about: Gives a transport adapter an opaque bearer lease for one profile/account, only for an exact resource origin the profile binds and only after allow_auth use and allow_credentials permits; a cached token is reused, otherwise one coordinated acquisition/refresh runs per credential identity. Never starts an interactive flow.

todos.todo: Require allow_auth use for the caller profile/account and verify resource origin, requested scopes, audience binding and active account generation; reject absent login instead of initiating an interactive flow.

Use a valid cached credential or serialize token acquisition/refresh by principal, account, profile, audience and scope set; authorize token endpoint and storage effects, respect expiry skew and refresh rotation, and return a scope-bound opaque lease only to the adapter; invalid_grant requires login and ambiguous refresh never blindly replays.

failures.when: destination origin not listed in resource_origins
failures.code: auth.origin_not_bound (permission) returns; no token is fetched or attached

failures.when: scopes outside the profile or a different audience
missing allow_auth use or allow_credentials
failures.code: permission.denied before the store or token endpoint is touched

use_cases.name: begin_authorization
use_cases.label: Begin authorization
use_cases.about: Starts a principal-bound authorization-code (PKCE S256) or device transaction for one profile/account after allow_auth manage and allow_credentials permits; returns only challenge data (authorization URL or user code), never a verifier, state secret or token, and never opens a browser.

todos.todo: Resolve a configured OAuth profile and caller-owned account; reject unsupported grant types, unapproved redirect URIs, scope expansion and missing allow_auth or credential-store grants before creating transaction state.

Through OAuthSessionDriver mint bounded principal-bound state and PKCE S256 verifier for authorization code, or request a device code through an authorized endpoint; retain secrets in the transaction store and return only an expiring authorization URL or user-code challenge; never launch a browser implicitly.

failures.when: begin on a client_credentials profile
missing allow_auth manage or allow_credentials
failures.code: permission.denied before any state or network

use_cases.name: cancel_authorization
use_cases.label: Cancel a pending authorization
use_cases.about: Invalidates one of the caller's open authorization transactions (state, verifier and device code are discarded, the provider is never contacted); idempotent, and a transaction that already ended reports its terminal state unchanged.

todos.todo: rivet.auth.cancel {transaction_id}: resolve the transaction through OAuthSessionDriver and bind it to the authenticated principal that began it (principal-bound); a transaction owned by another principal, or an unknown id, is not_found (exit 4, HTTP 404) without disclosing that it exists. Requires allow_auth manage for the transaction's profile.

Invalidate the pending transaction through OAuthSessionDriver.cancel: discard its state, PKCE verifier and device code so a later rivet.auth.complete for it fails, stop any in-flight device poll owned by the calling request, and never contact the provider. Return AuthCancelReceipt{transaction_id, state:"cancelled"}.

Idempotent: cancelling an already-cancelled transaction returns the same receipt; a transaction that already reached a terminal state (connected, denied, expired) returns {transaction_id, state:<that terminal state>} unchanged and does not revoke stored credentials (use rivet.auth.disconnect for that). No token material, state or verifier appears in the receipt or the trace.

failures.when: unknown or foreign transaction

use_cases.name: complete_authorization
use_cases.label: Complete authorization
use_cases.about: Completes the caller's own authorization transaction: a code callback is checked (state, redirect URI, issuer, TTL, single use) before the PKCE code exchange; a device transaction polls the token endpoint under the request deadline and answers {"state":"pending"} without consuming the transaction when the deadline comes first. Returns sanitized CredentialStatus, never tokens.

todos.todo: Verify transaction ownership, expiry, configured issuer, exact redirect URI, single-use state and callback or device-poll mode; reject mismatch before token exchange and never log codes or device credentials.

Exchange authorization code with its PKCE verifier or poll the device token endpoint at the required interval under the request deadline. If wait:true reaches the request deadline while the provider still says pending, return {"state":"pending"} and do NOT consume the transaction; only explicit auth cancel or expiry invalidates it. On success persist rotated credentials atomically through the authorized store, consume transaction state, and return sanitized account status instead of tokens; preserve denial, expiry and uncertain exchange errors.

failures.when: unknown id or another principal's transaction
missing callback for a code transaction, or a callback on a device transaction

use_cases.name: credential_status
use_cases.label: Credential status
use_cases.about: Reports the caller's own account state for one profile (connected, expired or disconnected, granted scopes, expiry, generation) after allow_auth status and allow_credentials read permits; never refreshes, discovers endpoints or returns token material.

todos.todo: Bind profile and account to the authenticated principal and require status authority; reject cross-tenant identifiers without disclosing their existence.
Read only the authorized credential entry through OAuthSessionDriver and report connection state, granted scopes and expiry; do not refresh, discover endpoints or return token material.

failures.when: missing allow_auth status or allow_credentials read
failures.code: permission.denied before the store is read

use_cases.name: disconnect_account
use_cases.label: Disconnect account
use_cases.about: Forgets the caller's local credentials for one profile/account: cancels its open transactions, removes stored tokens, advances the generation so no new lease uses the old one, and reports local_only true (no provider revocation is claimed).

todos.todo: Require ownership and disconnect authority for the account, cancel its active authorization transactions and prevent new credential leases from that generation.

Delete the local stored credentials and advance the account generation through OAuthSessionDriver; report local_only true because remote provider revocation is not implied, and refuse success if durable deletion fails.

failures.when: missing manage or credential-store grant

Initialize or acquire the scoped MCP session, forward validated input with new correlation IDs, preserve content and structured results, and map protocol/tool errors distinctly; propagate cancellation and clean up owned sessions.

the MCP endpoint answers 401 to a bearer

use_cases.name: exchange_datagrams
use_cases.label: Exchange datagrams
use_cases.about: Validates one step of a scoped UDP socket (open, send, send_to, receive, receive_from, close), authorizes every peer, listener bind and multicast join it implies before the socket exists or a packet leaves, then runs the step on the scope's own socket through DatagramDriver.

todos.todo: Validate peer, local bind, interface, datagram size and multicast options; require outbound network and any explicit listen grants before creating the socket, and treat implicit ephemeral client binds as part of the exact peer permit.

Drive bounded sends and receives through DatagramDriver; preserve datagram boundaries and sender metadata, reject truncation, do not infer delivery or replay lost messages, and close the scope on completion, timeout or cancellation; leave multicast groups during cleanup.

failures.when: a peer, bind, group or join intent is denied, or a resolved private address is not granted literally
an incoming datagram exceeds max_datagram
no datagram before the receive deadline

use_cases.name: cancel_request
use_cases.label: Cancel a running request
use_cases.about: Signals cancellation of a caller's own running top-level request; the request's structured cancellation token fires, its scope closes every open handle in reverse order within the 5 s grace, reaps child processes, and its caller receives one `cancelled` error (exit 130). Idempotent; never reveals other principals' requests.

todos.todo: Check request ownership and distinguish an unknown request from an already terminal request without exposing another principal's request.
Signal the shared cancellation tree through RequestControl and return an idempotent acknowledgement; completion remains pending until cleanup finishes.

failures.when: unknown or foreign request id

use_cases.name: request_operation
use_cases.label: Request an operation
use_cases.about: The one dispatcher every surface uses: resolves the ID, rejects unknown/invalid params before injecting defaults, enforces call depth, drives the compiled body in a supervised scope, validates the result against the declared output and returns exactly one Completion or error.

todos.todo: Resolve ID and snapshot, reject unauthorized operation and unknown or invalid input fields before injecting defaults. Derive the child deadline, carry parent_request_id for nested requests and accept/emit W3C traceparent on HTTP surfaces. Intersect host ceiling, loaded policy.json and any per-request restriction (callers can only narrow). Refuse before scheduling when nested depth exceeds limits.max_call_depth (limit.call_depth), when the host-wide limits.max_concurrent_requests budget (default 64, shared by nested calls and DAG nodes) is exhausted (429 limit), or when limits.max_buffered_bytes (default 256 MiB) cannot reserve the request's queues.
Drive the compiled plan through the injected driver; validate each data frame, await callback demand, and propagate cancellation without replaying emitted data.

Join the request scope through ScopeSupervisor (await child cancellation and bounded resource cleanup in reverse acquisition order). Validate the final result against the operation's declared OutputSpec via validate_output BEFORE building the Completion; on mismatch return kind output_invalid, code output.invalid (HTTP 500, exit 5) with effects preserved. Return exactly one completion or primary error with suppressed cleanup errors and committed-effect status.

failures.when: nesting deeper than limits.max_call_depth
an operation that `receives` input cannot run as a plain unary request
an emitted item violates `emits`
failures.code: output.invalid (500, exit 5) with details.seq and the run's effects

use_cases.name: run_dag
use_cases.label: Run a DAG
use_cases.about: Schedules declared nodes by their `after` edges within the dag `limit`: ready nodes run concurrently, failed or blocked dependencies block descendants, `fail fast` (the default) cancels running nodes and skips the rest, `fail independent` lets unaffected branches finish, and every node ends with a status envelope.

todos.todo: Reject cycles, ambiguous side-effect ordering and invalid references; assign nodes deterministic identities, attach per-node deadlines and effect requirements, and default the failure policy to `fail fast` when the dag header omits it. Every node starts pending.

Move a node pending->ready when all dependencies succeeded, then ready->running while the dag `limit` and the host-wide limits.max_concurrent_requests budget allow. A node whose dependency failed or was blocked becomes blocked. Under fail fast, the first failure cancels running nodes (-> cancelled) and marks never-started nodes skipped; under the retaining policy independent branches continue. Join every child through ScopeSupervisor before returning.

Expose each node's value as the envelope {status, result, error}; `.result` of a non-succeeded node is null. Return DagCompletion{result, nodes:[{id, status, error?, started_at?, ended_at?}], effects} where status is one of succeeded, failed, blocked, skipped, cancelled.

failures.when: the dag timeout expired
failures.code: timeout.dag becomes the fatal error; running nodes are cancelled

failures.when: under fail fast the first failure becomes the fatal error and stops scheduling

use_cases.name: validate_output
use_cases.label: Validate a result against its declared output
use_cases.about: Pure structural check of a final result against the operation's OutputSpec before any Completion is built; a mismatch becomes output.invalid with committed effects preserved.

todos.todo: If the declared output type is json (opaque, including the default when no output line exists), return valid=true without a structural check.

Otherwise walk the result against the OutputSpec: scalar type must match (integer accepts only whole numbers; bytes must be base64); every required field must be present and non-null; optional fields may be absent; a closed object rejects any extra key; `list T` checks every element; nested objects recurse. Collect each violation as {path, expected, actual} (at most 32, then truncate with a count).

Return OutputVerdict{valid, violations}. When invalid also build RivetError{kind output_invalid, code output.invalid, retryable false, effects copied from the check input so committed effects stay reported}. Pure: no ports, no I/O, never mutates the result.

failures.when: result violates the declared output
failures.code: output.invalid (HTTP 500, exit 5) returned in the verdict

use_cases.name: apply_file_operation
use_cases.label: Apply a file operation
use_cases.about: Authorizes every path the verb touches (source, destination) with its access verb before any handle opens, then performs the confined create/read/update/append/delete/list/stat/copy/move through FileAccess.

todos.todo: Validate create/read/update/delete mode, size bounds and version guards; request authorization for each source, destination and temporary path before opening handles.

Apply through FileAccess with directory-relative confinement; create exclusively, update only existing files with atomic replacement when supported, and delete only explicitly named entries. use_cases.name: compile_program

The grammar is Capy prefix calls: (request "id" {k: v}), (request.stream "id" {...}), named arguments as a trailing object, `x = (f a b)` and `node n after [a, b] = (request ...)`; durations are quoted strings matching ^[0-9]+(ms|s|m|h)$; ${...} holds dotted paths only; string escapes are limited to \n \t \" \\ \xNN \uNNNN.

Operations of a module that no chain of `public` imports reaches become private (internal: callable inside the bundle, never listed). Connector and auth profile names stay bundle-unique (the loader's policy grants them by name; a duplicate across files is check.import_collision) and each file may reference only its own.

Lower each operation's output/emits/receives declarations through compile_output_spec and attach the resulting OutputSpec (plus its declared errors) to the RegistryEntry. Reject duplicate IDs across the bundle atomically with both source spans (registry.duplicate_id, exit 2) and build one immutable catalog for every surface, including the built-ins rivet.list, rivet.describe, rivet.outputs, rivet.request and rivet.sessions.*. With strict_docs, reject blank public operation/parameter descriptions, a missing output description on any public operation, a missing description on any output/emits/receives field, and undeclared fail codes. Validate gRPC descriptor methods and cardinality without reflection or protoc I/O.

Resolve operation IDs, types, lexical ownership and DAG edges without executing anything. Enforce header order (name, description, private, param*, output(+block), emits, receives, error*) and the leading-options rule: an option line after the first body statement of an operation or of a with/http/grpc block is syntax.option_after_body. Reject duplicate IDs, unknown options, DAG cycles, escaping handles, `while` without a finite enclosing deadline, and `return` used to produce a map/poll value (those bodies must `yield`). Detect static call cycles over literal (request "id" ...) targets (check.call_cycle). Warn when a `return` reads node.result without a status guard. Lower URL interpolation as component-aware (path segment vs query value; never adds segments, ?, # or @) and bind every `secret ... from env ... for ORIGIN` to its origins. Validate OAuth profiles, declared token stores, QUIC ALPN and stream ownership, UDP modes and HTTP version/fallback choices; include token refresh, credential storage, UDP binds and QUIC migration in the static effect graph.

Turn each grantable site into a (capability, target) pair: exact targets as written (./out/user.json, udp://127.0.0.1:7000, crm/tools/search, env name); param_dependent URLs collapse to their origin scheme://host:port; param_dependent paths become their derived glob (./out/notes/*.json); bounded targets use their bound set. Without an output path return the draft (CLI prints it to stdout; HTTP POST /v1/policy/generate, MCP rivet.policy.generate and Runtime::generate_policy return {policy, review, complete} and never write files). With --output ask PolicyDraftWriter.write_new, which creates the file exclusively and refuses an existing path with conflict.exists (exit 4) so a reviewed policy is never overwritten. List each review site on stderr (operation, kind, target, knowledge, source). Exit 7 when review is non-empty (the draft is still produced/written), else 0. use_cases.name: load_policy
use_cases.label: Load policy.json
use_cases.about: Finds policy.json beside the entry file (or the file named by --policy PATH), validates schema v1 strictly and returns the effective Policy. No file means deny-by-default for every new application effect; pure operations still run.

todos.todo: If the caller passed --policy PATH (a path only, never grant text) use exactly that file; otherwise ask PolicyFileReader.discover for policy.json in the directory of the entry .rivet file. No environment variable is consulted. An explicit path that does not exist is config error policy.invalid (exit 2); an absent auto-discovered file is not an error.

When no file is found, return Policy{source absent, grants [], deny [], network.deny_private_ranges true, default limits (64 concurrent, depth 16, 256 MiB), serve none} so pure operations still run and every new application I/O is denied. Read the bytes (PolicyFileReader.read, which also records sha256) and parse strict JSON. Require version == 1. Intersect the parsed grants with the host ceiling when a library host supplied one (a file can never widen it), compute policy_hash over the canonical JSON, and return the immutable Policy used by authorize_effect, start_serve and every request context.

use_cases.name: project_polling
use_cases.label: Project polling
use_cases.about: The HTTP polling routes are a projection of the session operations: open → 202 SessionReceipt with events_url, events → SessionBatch, input/finish_input/cancel → SessionAck / CancelReceipt, all bound to the authenticated principal.

todos.todo: POST /v1/requests {id, params} -> SessionDriver.open and return 202 SessionReceipt with events_url=/v1/requests/{session_id}/events. Unary operations may be submitted the same way as async jobs; their batch carries one terminal result event.
GET /v1/requests/{id}/events?after_seq=N&wait_ms=M -> SessionDriver.read (sessions.read) and return 200 SessionBatch; wait_ms is capped by the host maximum and returns early when events arrive.
POST /v1/requests/{id}/input -> SessionDriver.send; POST .../finish_input -> SessionDriver.finish_input; POST .../cancel -> SessionDriver.cancel returning a CancelReceipt that includes session_id.

Every route checks that the session belongs to the authenticated principal; another principal's or an expired session is 404. Sessions are principal-owned and survive client reconnects until idle/total expiry.

failures.when: the principal may not call the operation

use_cases.name: start_serve
use_cases.label: Start serve
use_cases.about: Binds one listener and mounts every enabled surface (REST, SSE, polling, WebSocket, MCP) on it, refusing an unauthenticated non-loopback bind; `--stdio` serves MCP only and binds nothing.

todos.todo: `rivet serve --stdio` serves MCP over stdio only (a stdio pipe cannot share a socket) and skips binding. Otherwise listen on --listen ADDR (default 127.0.0.1:8080). There are no --transport or --mcp flags.

Read serve.auth from the loaded policy (missing serve.auth = type none). If auth is none and the listen address is not loopback, refuse to start with serve.auth_required (exit 2) before binding anything.
Enabled surfaces = policy serve.surfaces or, when absent, all five: http, sse, poll, ws, mcp. A disabled surface's routes are not mounted and answer 404.

Bind once through ServeListener.bind, then mount each enabled surface on that one listener: http (POST /v1/request, GET /v1/operations, GET /v1/operations/{id}, GET /v1/operations/{id}/outputs), sse (POST /v1/request with Accept: text/event-stream), poll (POST /v1/requests, GET /v1/requests/{id}/events, POST /v1/requests/{id}/input|finish_input|cancel), ws (GET /v1/ws, subprotocol rivet.v1) and mcp (POST|GET|DELETE /mcp, Streamable HTTP). Every mount shares the same immutable catalog, dispatcher and broker and the same authenticate -> authorize path. If any mount fails, close the listener and return the error; never serve a partial surface set silently.

Return ServeReceipt{listen_addr, stdio, surfaces, auth_type, catalog_version, policy_hash}. With no policy.json serve still starts (loopback, auth none): pure operations work and all effects are denied.

failures.when: --listen is not HOST:PORT
auth none and a non-loopback --listen
serve.auth type mtls
a surface fails to mount
failures.code: the adapter's error and nothing is served

use_cases.name: parse_input
use_cases.label: Parse input envelope
use_cases.about: Turns one JSON request body (HTTP /v1/request and /v1/requests, a WebSocket request frame, the MCP rivet.request and rivet.sessions.open arguments, `rivet request --input FILE|-` / `--data`, the library's Runtime::call_json and the FFI) into the one InputEnvelope {operation, data, deadline_ms?, restrict?, stream?}; the 0.1.0 keys id/params are deprecated aliases through 0.2.x and are reported so each surface can emit its deprecation signal.

examples.result: validation.input_envelope (exit 2, HTTP 422): use `operation` or the deprecated `id`, not both

todos.todo: The body must be a JSON object; any other JSON value is validation.input_envelope. An `error` key is refused with validation.input_envelope (an input envelope never carries an error). Unknown keys are ignored as in 0.1.0 (WS frames keep type/ref beside the envelope).

`operation` (non-empty string) names the operation. The deprecated alias `id` is read only when legacy_ok (always true in 0.2.x, false from 0.3.0); `operation` and `id` together is validation.input_envelope `use `operation` or the deprecated `id`, not both`; neither is validation.required with details.field = "operation" (0.1.0 code and exit status kept); a non-string value is validation.input_envelope.

`data` is the operation input and defaults to {} when absent or null; the deprecated alias `params` is read only when legacy_ok; `data` and `params` together is validation.input_envelope `use `data` or the deprecated `params`, not both`.

Optional deadline_ms (non-negative integer, clamped to 1..=600000 as in 0.1.0), restrict (passed through; the runtime validates it as policy grants), stream (bool) and pretty (bool, honoured by the FFI); a wrong type for any of them is validation.input_envelope naming the key.

Return InputEnvelope with `aliases` listing every deprecated key that was used ("id", "params"), so the surface emits its deprecation signal: HTTP `Deprecation: true` plus `deprecated=1` in the access log, a CLI `warning[deprecated.input]` line on stderr, and a trace note. Pure: no ports, no I/O.

failures.when: the body is not a JSON object or carries an `error` key
`operation` with `id`, or `data` with `params`
neither `operation` nor `id`

use_cases.name: cancel_session
use_cases.label: Cancel session
use_cases.about: Cancels the session's owned request tree, awaits bounded cleanup and returns a CancelReceipt; the cancelled terminal event stays readable during retention.

todos.todo: Check principal and session ownership before accessing live state; treat repeated cancellation as idempotent while distinguishing unknown/expired state without cross-principal disclosure.

Signal the owned request cancellation tree through SessionDriver, stop input acceptance and await bounded protocol/resource cleanup; return a CancelReceipt carrying session_id and request_id; preserve committed effects and a final cancelled/error event for the retention period.

failures.when: session_id is empty

use_cases.name: finish_input
use_cases.label: Finish input
use_cases.about: Half-closes the session's input: already accepted messages drain, then `for message in incoming` ends; output keeps flowing until the terminal event.

todos.todo: Authorize the live session and serialize with sends; reject unknown or expired sessions and preserve an idempotent already-finished response.

Mark input closed after already accepted messages, ask SessionDriver to deliver protocol half-close, and continue receiving output until terminal status or cancellation; this does not dispose the enclosing resource.

failures.when: session_id is empty

use_cases.name: open_session
use_cases.label: Open session
use_cases.about: Opens a bounded, principal-owned request lifetime for any public operation (streaming or unary) and returns the SessionReceipt with the pinned catalog version, input/emits schemas and the first send sequence.

todos.todo: Resolve the caller-visible operation and parameter/input/output schemas; pin catalog version, principal, policy and deadline; enforce per-principal session and queue limits before scheduling any child effects.

Create a host-owned bounded child request scope and opaque principal-bound session ID through SessionDriver; return schema and sequence cursors without exposing handles; expire and cancel the scope on idle or total deadline.

failures.when: id is empty
params is not an object

use_cases.name: read_events
use_cases.label: Read events
use_cases.about: Long-polls the session's ordered event log after a cursor; `after_seq` acknowledges delivered events so they can be evicted, and exactly one terminal result/error ends the sequence.

todos.todo: Authorize single-consumer access; validate after_seq against retained and previously delivered events, acknowledge only known delivered events, and reject future or expired cursors rather than pretending data exists.

Read up to max_events under bounded wait through SessionDriver, preserving event order and one terminal result/error; retain unacknowledged events for bounded replay, apply producer backpressure and report gaps explicitly.

failures.when: session_id is empty

use_cases.name: send_input
use_cases.label: Send input
use_cases.about: Enqueues one input message for an operation that declares `receives`; the acknowledgement proves local queue acceptance only.

todos.todo: Authorize session ownership and current operation access; reject completed input, wrong input schema, out-of-order send_seq or queue byte overflow before enqueue; a retry of the most recent sequence is accepted only for the identical payload hash.

Await queue capacity within the action deadline and enqueue through SessionDriver, then acknowledge local acceptance; never claim remote processing and never re-send an already acknowledged sequence to gRPC.

failures.when: send_seq is 0

use_cases.name: exchange_http
use_cases.label: Exchange http
use_cases.about: One brokered HTTP exchange: encodes the typed body, authorizes the origin and every resolved address before dialing, sends through the connection-level client at the declared HTTP version (`version 3` strict HTTP/3, `version prefer [3, 2]` falling back only before any request byte), re-authorizes each redirect hop (only when `redirect follow` is set), retries only replay-safe methods on listed statuses, then maps a non-accepted status to http.status and decodes the body.

todos.todo: Build method, URL, headers and body from the lowered `http` block; URL interpolation was already encoded per component at compile time. Require the allow_network permit for scheme://host:port (and allow_auth / allow_credentials when an OAuth lease is attached) before any connection.

Send through HttpClient under the request deadline with the declared HTTP version/fallback; every redirect hop is re-authorized as a new target. Propagate W3C traceparent when the caller supplied one.

Decode the body through Codec per the block's `decode` option (json/text/bytes). A non-2xx status the operation does not map with catch/accept status becomes code http.status with details.status (kind http, exit 5, 502).

more hops than `redirect follow limit N`

the H3 request may already have reached the server (bytes written, response lost)
failures.code: its connection error and nothing is re-sent over TCP, whatever the method

use_cases.name: exchange_socket
use_cases.label: Exchange socket
use_cases.about: Opens one scope-owned duplex connection (TCP, Unix socket or WebSocket) after refusing Stage C options, authorizing the endpoint (allow_network connect for tcp/ws/wss, allow_unix connect for a socket path) and checking every resolved address; framing and message exchange then run through the returned connection until the scope closes it.

todos.todo: Require allow_network for ws(s)://host:port or tcp://host:port (plus allow_listen for any bind) before connecting; WebSocket performs the TLS/upgrade handshake, TCP connects raw or with TLS.
Exchange messages through SocketStream with explicit framing from Codec (WebSocket messages, or length-prefix/newline framing for TCP), bounded per-direction queues and deadline-counted flow control.
On completion, error or cancel: WebSocket sends a close handshake within grace, TCP half-closes then closes; the socket never outlives its lexical scope.

failures.when: `tls` on tcp/unix or `reconnect`
endpoint or resolved address not granted

use_cases.name: run_process
use_cases.label: Run process
use_cases.about: Runs one argv-only child: refuses shell strings and PATH lookups, authorizes allow_exec on the exact binary, requires an OS sandbox whenever policy.json is present (built from the policy's read/write/exec grants; unrepresentable grants or a missing backend fail before spawning), encodes stdin, and maps a nonzero exit to kind process unless `accept exit` lists it.

todos.todo: Require allow_exec naming the exact program path; argv is a list (no shell), environment starts empty and adds only allow_env-granted variables; cwd must be inside a granted directory.
Run through ProcessRunner with bounded stdout/stderr capture and the request deadline; stdin receives only declared input.

On deadline or cancel close stdin, terminate, then kill after grace and always reap; return exit status and captured output, mapping a non-zero exit to kind dependency (exit 5) unless the operation accepts it.

failures.when: exit not accepted
